title.narrative: SPVO - BRIDGE: Building Responsible, Inclusive, and Dignified Global Employment

description.narrative: Led by Verité in partnership with ofi Ghana Ltd., this two-year pilot initiative establishes a scalable model to embed fair labor and ethical recruitment practices across Ghana’s cocoa and cashew sectors, two of the country’s most critical export industries where systemic risks threaten both worker welfare and access to global markets. Despite legal frameworks such as Labor Act 651, ARS-1000, and Rainforest Alliance (RA) standards, farm-level employment remains predominantly informal, leaving hundreds of thousands of workers, particularly women and migrant laborers, vulnerable to exploitation, unsafe conditions, and inconsistent wages. These vulnerabilities expose supply chains to regulatory and reputational risks under the EU Deforestation Regulation (EUDR) and Corporate Sustainability Due Diligence Directive (CSDDD).Taking a bottom-up, evidence-driven approach, the BRIDGE project first embeds fair-labor training content directly into the existing curricula and delivery systems of the Ghana Cocoa Board’s (COCOBOD) Farmer Business School, the Tree Crops Development Authority (TCDA), and the Ministry of Food & Agriculture (MoFA) extension services, ensuring that fair labor, ethical recruitment, child labor prevention, and occupational safety practices become part of standardized, long-term instruction across cocoa and cashew regions. Main activities:Stakeholder Analysis, Curriculum Review, and Cashew Sector Rapid Appraisal• Objective: Build a shared understanding of sector dynamics and labor challenges across the cocoa and cashew industries. Identify key stakeholders and assess opportunities to integrate safe labor practices, gender-sensitive approaches, and child labor prevention into training and extension curricula for both sectors.Direct Pilot Training for Cocoa & Cashew Producers• Objective: Field-test and refine sector-specific labor training materials.Training of Trainers (ToT) for Stakeholders• Objective: Training of (60) trainers to build sustainable, decentralised capacity to deliver labor training across commodities.Step-Down Trainings with Producers• Objective: Cascade labor training to farmers by the Training-of-Trainers (ToT), workers, and community members through institutionalised channels.Farm- and Industry-Level Toolkits• Objective: Provide practical tools for farm-level and industry-level adoption of safe labor practices.
